newsitem.title: UK: Racal seeks telecoms partner,mulls selloffs.
newsitem.headline: Racal seeks telecoms partner,mulls selloffs.

text.p: Racal Electronics Plc vowed to do better for shareholders on Tuesday, after reporting a sharp fall in headline profits and said it was now seeking partnerships for its British-based telecoms network business as well as considering sell-offs of other parts of the group.
Chairman Sir Ernest Harrison told a news conference that the company was undervalued and he was looking at all the options to increase shareholder value.
He did not rule out keeping all three of the core telecoms, data communication products and defence electronics businesses and growing them in-house.

But he said mergers and acquisitions specialists were being appointed to advise the firm on the possibilities of joining forces to develop its telecoms business, where it had sales of 260 million pounds last year.
Options to be looked at include teaming up with overseas players weaving global alliances, such as AT&T or other European operators seeking to break out of their domestic markets.

Separately, the company had retained investment bank Goldman Sachs to advise on strategy for its newly restructured data communications products division but he could not say if or when any deals would get done.
"All options are open," Harrison said. "We will work on it but they have to be deals which are in the shareholders' interest and it may take some time."
More immediately, the company hoped its troubled data products division was on track to move back into profit, following a radical restructuring and the launch of a range of new products.

Earlier, the company reported pretax profits fell to 40.4 million pounds for the year to March 31 from 70.4 million pounds last year, with the fall largely due to restructuring costs of 29 million pounds at Data Products division.
Group sales were up 142 million pounds at 1.138 billion pounds but Data Products made an operating loss of 19.1 million pounds on sales of 281 million pounds.

The company said the division was now introducing a range of new products, that had been delayed by technical problems, which should now start to bring in $70 million a year of additional "high margin" income.

"One thing which will dramatically change our profitability is data products," Harrison told the news conference. "The most immediate key (to increasing shareholder value) is Data Products coming good."
